name: agenttelemetry-bench
description: AgentTelemetry: a fault-detection benchmark and dataset for LLM-agent observability. Contains (1) controlled fault-injection traces across 14 fault types x 5 observability conditions x 7 framework adapters; (2) 112 SWE-bench Lite case-study traces (3,060 spans, 9 span kinds, full attribute capture, GUARD_RAIL verification labels); (3) 159-run real-LLM validation traces across 13 production-tier models with organic-anomaly labels. All traces use OTLP-compatible JSONL with agenttelemetry.span.kind as a string attribute on standard OpenTelemetry INTERNAL spans.
citeAs: @inproceedings{agenttelemetry2026, title={AgentTelemetry: A Fault Detection Benchmark and Toolkit for LLM Agent Observability}, author={Balusu, Krishna Chaitanya}, booktitle={ACM AIware 2026, Benchmark & Dataset Track}, year={2026}}
rai:dataCollection: Three sub-corpora collected via distinct mechanisms: (1) Controlled corpus generated synthetically by the AgentTelemetry FaultInjector module at benchmark time using deterministic mock LLM clients (input-hash to fixed response); no human labeling, no live API calls. (2) SWE-bench corpus generated by running a ReAct coding agent on princeton-nlp/SWE-bench_Lite (37% sample, all 12 repos) using GPT-4o-mini at $0.001/run. (3) Real-LLM corpus produced by running a fixed research-assistant prompt against 13 production-tier models from Anthropic and OpenAI; total spend $0.62.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Controlled corpus has ground-truth fault-type labels generated by the injector. SWE-bench corpus has per-instance reasoning-loop / tool-failure attribution labels and ground-truth diff comparison via LLM-judged file/code/approach matching (87.9% plausibility, official SWE-bench harness verification queued). Real-LLM corpus has per-run organic-anomaly labels manually verified for true positive / false positive (precision = 1.000 on 4 organic infinite_retry alerts).
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Maintained by the producer at https://github.com/Krishnachaitanyakc/AgentTelemetry. Versioned with semver; new fault types and framework adapters added in minor releases. Issue tracker on GitHub for community contributions.
rai:dataLifeCycle: Initial release coincides with the AIware 2026 paper. Future releases will add: (a) official SWE-bench harness verification results; (b) larger-sample matched-control intervention results; (c) controlled human user-study results; (d) traces from additional agent frameworks as adapters are added.
rai:dataUseCases: Intended uses: benchmarking observability tools for LLM agents; teaching agent failure modes; building closed-loop runtime safeguards; OTel SemConv standardization input. Out-of-scope: training policy models on the trace corpus (the corpus is too small and synthetic for policy learning).
rai:dataBiases: The Custom-adapter corpus uses reference-implementation instrumentation; the other six adapters use manual instrumentation stubs that may not exercise full framework behavior. SWE-bench traces use a single GPT-4o-mini agent and may not generalize to larger or different-architecture agents (e.g., tree-of-thought, hierarchical multi-agent). Real-LLM corpus skews toward short tasks (median 3.0 iterations, 4,768 input tokens for Haiku 4.5).
rai:dataLimitations: Controlled corpus uses deterministic mocks; the model dimension contributes no independent signal under mocks (real-LLM corpus addresses this with 13 models). The 159-run real-LLM corpus does not exercise all 14 fault types organically; only missing_guardrail reaches FDR=1.000 organically (cost_explosion 0.538, wrong_tool 0.154, tool_failure 0.000, context_overflow 0.000). The closed-loop intervention sample (n=24 per arm) is underpowered (Fisher's exact p=0.53); larger-sample replication queued.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Positive: faster fault diagnosis for safety-critical agent deployments; structured telemetry enables runtime guardrails; common vocabulary for failure analysis. Negative externality to consider: fine-grained REASONING and PLANNING spans capture model chain-of-thought, which may contain user PII or proprietary prompt content in production deployments. Mitigation: three-level privacy model (NONE/METADATA_ONLY/FULL) with METADATA_ONLY default; FDR is identical at metadata and full capture levels for fault detection. Released traces use synthetic fault-injection inputs and contain no human-subject data.
rai:dataSensitivePersonalInformation: None. The benchmark uses synthetic prompts and the SWE-bench traces use already-public GitHub issue text from princeton-nlp/SWE-bench_Lite. No human-subject data, no PII, no protected-class attributes.
